claims.text: A 61-year-old woman with dyslipidemia, hypertension and obesity consulted her dermatologist for a budding peri-umbilical skin lesion that had appeared six months before. She reported unintentional weight loss, deterioration of her overall health, repeated metrorrhagia and diffuse abdominopelvic pain. Examination showed a WHO performance index of 3 and a painful, ulcerated, oozing 3 cm umbilical nodule with low-abundance ascites and tumor-like hepatomegaly.

claims.text: Biological tests showed severe hypochromic microcytic iron deficiency anemia at 3.5 g/dl and increased tumor markers including ACE. Pelvic ultrasound, thoraco-abdominopelvic CT and abdominopelvic MRI showed an enlarged uterus with a very thickened endometrium, secondary lesions of the lungs, liver and digestive tract, and pelvic iliac and lumboaortic lymphadenopathies. Endometrial biopsy and curettage after transfusion of 4 globular pellets confirmed well differentiated endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma.
